defects.subcategory: Wrong update formula in spec (and matching wrong gold): damped Jacobi missing the (1-omega) relaxation term, fixed in prompt and recomputed in targets
defects.action: Corrected the weighted-Jacobi iteration formula in both the problem-level and step-level background, and recomputed the gold test values (r1) so they match the standard damped Jacobi.
defects.before_excerpt: x_i^{k+1} = \frac{b_i - \sum_{j\neq i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}}{a_{ii}\omega^{-1}}
defects.after_excerpt: x_i^{k+1} = (1-\omega)\,x_i^{(k)} + \omega\,\frac{b_i - \sum_{j\neq i}a_{ij}x_j^{(k)}}{a_{ii}}
defects.rationale: Both before_excerpt and after_excerpt are verbatim from field_diffs (field_diffs[0] problem_background_main and field_diffs[1] step 9.1 step_background carry identical text). The original formula b_i - sum.../(a_ii*omega^{-1}) = omega*(standard Jacobi update)/a_ii, omitting the (1-omega)x_i^{(k)} damping term; it is correct only at omega=1 and gives wrong iterates for omega=2/3 and omega=0.5. The verified text is the standard weighted/damped Jacobi x^{k+1}=(1-omega)x^k+omega*D^{-1}(b-Rx^k). The target_patch note confirms gold for test0 (omega=2/3) and test2 (omega=0.5) was recomputed with the corrected formula in r1; test1 (omega=1) was left out of the patch since the two formulas agree there (h5 original retained, independent recompute allclose ~1e-13). defects.subcategory: under-specified coupling convention (J symmetry + zero diagonal not stated)
defects.action: Replaced the bare scaling definition with the explicit symmetric, zero-diagonal construction in both the main background and the step-50.4 background.
defects.before_excerpt: $J_{ij}\equiv n_{ij}/\sqrt{N}$, where $n_{ij}$'s are i.i.d. from $N(0,1)$.
defects.after_excerpt: the couplings are generated as A = np.random.randn(N, N); J = (A + A.T) / 2; np.fill_diagonal(J, 0); J = J / np.sqrt(N), i.e. $J_{ij} = (a_{ij}+a_{ji})/(2\sqrt{N})$ for $i \neq j$ and $J_{ii}=0$.
defects.rationale: field_diffs confirm both the main background and the step-50.4 background carried the under-specified convention $J_{ij}\equiv n_{ij}/\sqrt{N}$ (i.i.d. N(0,1)) with no statement that J is symmetric ($J_{ij}=J_{ji}$, required for the SK Hamiltonian to be well-defined) nor that the diagonal is zeroed (no self-interaction). The verified text makes the symmetric / zero-diagonal / 1/sqrt(N) construction explicit, matching what the hidden tests already built. Same convention fix in both fields -> grouped as one defect. before/after quoted directly from field_diffs.before/after.

defects.subcategory: allowed-np.random-function constraint pinning the RNG stream for seeded exact-spins tests
defects.action: Removed the 'only randint and rand are allowed' RNG constraint and rewrote the prompt to state only the equilibration task.
defects.before_excerpt: Use Monte Carlo method to find the thermal equilibrium state given an inital state and given interaction coefficients $J_{ij}$. If using functions from np.random, only "randint" and "rand" are allowed in this part.
defects.after_excerpt: Run single-spin-flip Metropolis Monte Carlo to bring `spins` to thermal equilibrium at temperature T under the couplings J, and return the equilibrated configuration.
defects.rationale: field_diffs.before contains the 'only randint and rand are allowed' clause verbatim. This is an artificial RNG-protocol constraint that pinned the exact random-number stream so the seeded exact-final-spins tests would reproduce bitwise; it constrains implementation, not physics. Ledger R3 (before_in_original=true) confirms it was load-bearing only for the deleted seeded exact-final-spins tests.

defects.subcategory: seeded exact-final-spins reproduction tests replaced by a statistical equilibration-energy test
defects.action: Replaced 3 seeded `np.allclose(spins, target)` exact-final-configuration tests with 1 statistical test asserting the mean equilibrated energy per spin lies within 3*0.0223 of REF=-0.4207.
defects.before_excerpt:
spins = find_equilibrium(spins, N, T, J, num_steps)
assert np.allclose(spins, target)
defects.after_excerpt:
energies.append(-0.5 * (spins @ J @ spins) / N)
assert (abs(np.mean(energies) - (-0.4207)) < 3 * 0.0223) == target
defects.rationale: field_diffs.before shows 3 tests each ending in `find_equilibrium(...)` then `assert np.allclose(spins, target)` -- asserting the exact final spin configuration, which only passes if the solver reproduces the gold MC RNG trajectory rather than reaching a correct equilibrium. field_diffs.after replaces them with a single statistical test on the equilibrated energy per spin with tolerance, accepting any correct equilibration. Ledger R3 / target_patch (before_in_original=true) confirm the redesign and its 18.9-sigma rejection margin.

defects.subcategory: allowed-np.random-function constraint pinning the RNG stream for seeded exact-(RSB,mean,std) tests

defects.after_excerpt: Calculate the mean and the population standard deviation (np.std with its default ddof=0) of the overall overlap distribution.
defects.rationale: field_diffs.before contains the 'only randn and choice are allowed' clause verbatim; an artificial RNG-protocol constraint that pinned the random stream so the seeded exact-(RSB,mean,std) reproduction tests would match bitwise. Ledger R3 (before_in_original=true) confirms it existed only to pin the RNG stream. The added '(np.std default ddof=0)' is a minor convention clarification of which std estimator to report.

defects.subcategory: seeded exact-(RSB,mean,std) reproduction tests replaced by statistical phase tests across the SK transition
defects.action: Replaced 3 seeded exact-(RSB,mean,std) `np.allclose` reproduction tests with 2 statistical phase tests (high-T replica-symmetric vs low-T spin-glass) checking RSB flag, |mean|, and std against physically motivated bounds.
defects.before_excerpt:

a, b, c = target
assert a == aa and np.allclose((b, c), (bb, cc))
defects.after_excerpt:
RSB, mean, std = spin_glass(N=50, T=1.5, num_steps=300, num_replicas=20, num_realizations=5)
assert ((RSB == False) and (abs(mean) < 0.05) and (std < 0.18)) == target
defects.rationale: field_diffs.before shows 3 tests requiring `a == aa and np.allclose((b,c),(bb,cc))` -- reproducing the exact (RSB,mean,std) triple to floating tolerance, which only passes under bitwise RNG reproduction of the gold protocol. field_diffs.after asserts the expected phase behaviour statistically (high T=1.5 -> no RSB, narrow overlaps; low T=0.5 -> RSB, broad overlaps). Ledger R3 / target_patch (before_in_original=true) confirm the redesign, ~6x cheaper params, and 0% across-seed failure.

defects.subcategory: return contract (RSB decision threshold) under-specified in prompt; relocated from theory background
defects.action: Stated the explicit return criterion (True if std(overlaps) > 1.4/sqrt(N) else False) in the prompt, and removed the 'allow some reasonable deviation in the judging criterion' hand-wave from the theory background.

defects.rationale: field_diffs #4 shows the original prompt stated no return contract (just 'analyze the overall overlap distribution'); the verified prompt adds the precise testable criterion std > 1.4/sqrt(N). field_diffs #5 shows the background's vague tail 'allow some reasonable deviation in the judging criterion' was removed, keeping physics motivation only. Both fields fix the same relocation of the return contract -> grouped. Ledger R3 (before_in_original=true) confirms moving the criterion from background to prompt. Clarity/spec-completeness fix, no easy-vs-strict valence.

Seeding the inputs hardens the test (test-robustness fix). No ledger note covers 50.3 test_cases -> inferred. Neutral-cleanup; not RNG over-specification of the solver (it pins the test input, not the implementation).

defects.subcategory: wrong/unreproducible gold from ill-conditioned positive (scattering) energies; replaced with well-conditioned bound-state (En<0) inputs + narrowed radius ranges, targets regenerated

Swapping to En<0 well-conditioned inputs makes integrators agree, and targets were regenerated (target_patch r1 touched 52.2 and 52.3). 52.3 inherits SolveSchroedinger; same underlying issue, grouped as one defect. Excerpts are faithful summaries of field_diffs.before/after.

defects.subcategory: added absolute tolerance (atol=1e-5) to bound-state-energy comparison for the shallowest, integrator-noise-sensitive roots
defects.action: Added atol=1e-5 to np.allclose(Bnd, target) in tests 1 and 2 so a correct solver is not rejected on the noise-sensitive shallowest bound-state energies.
defects.rationale: Anchored to field_diff sub_steps[3].test_cases tests 1 and 2, which add atol=1e-5 to np.allclose(Bnd, target). The shallowest bound-state energies are integrator-noise-sensitive (off by ~1e-7 at default rtol), so the default-tolerance np.allclose can wrongly reject a correct accurate solver; atol=1e-5 loosens minimally while still rejecting wrong energies. Confined to the substep test_cases: the general_tests copy (field_diff general_tests) leaves tests 1 and 2 unchanged at default tolerance, so general_tests is NOT in fields_involved. before/after quoted verbatim from field_diffs.

defects.after_excerpt: assert np.isclose(Bnd[0], (0,-1)).all() == target.all()
defects.rationale: Anchored to field_diff sub_steps[3].test_cases test 3 AND field_diff general_tests test 3, both changing .any()==target.any() to .all()==target.all(). With target=[True,True], target.any()=True and np.isclose(Bnd[0],(0,-1)).any() is True whenever the first state's l==0 regardless of its energy, so e.g. Bnd[0]=(0,42.0) passes; the test adds essentially no constraint. .all() requires both l and E to match. Same change in both fields, grouped. before/after quoted verbatim from field_diffs.

defects.subcategory: ambiguous/misleading rounding convention ('rounded up' -> round-to-nearest)
defects.action: Replaced the ambiguous phrase 'rounded up to one decimal point' with 'rounded to one decimal place (round-to-nearest)' everywhere the periodicity output is specified (problem_io and the 53.3/53.4 docstrings).
defects.before_excerpt: prey_period: estimated periodicity of prey population, float rounded up to one decimal point.
defects.after_excerpt: prey_period: estimated periodicity of prey population, float rounded to one decimal place (round-to-nearest).
defects.rationale: Anchored: field_diffs for problem_io, 53.3.function_header and 53.4.function_header all carry the identical 'rounded up to one decimal point' -> 'rounded to one decimal place (round-to-nearest)' change. 'rounded up' literally reads as ceiling, whereas the gold uses ordinary round-to-nearest at one decimal place; clarifying the convention is the genuine fix. The change neither hand-holds nor tightens the task on its own, so neutral-cleanup is appropriate. Three mirrored docstrings making the same edit are correctly grouped as one conceptual defect.

defects.subcategory: wrong PDF formula (inverted exponential rate) + under-specified sampling scale
defects.action: Corrected the exponential waiting-time PDF in the background from f=(1/a)exp(-dt/a) to f=a*exp(-a*dt), and folded the load-bearing sampling convention 'scale=1/a (mean waiting time, a=sum a_i)' into the 53.1 prompt instead of the vague 'use NumPy's exponential distribution directly'.
defects.before_excerpt: $$f(\Delta t) = \frac{1}{a} \exp\left(-\frac{\Delta t}{a}\right)$$ where $a = \sum a_i$. ... use NumPy's exponential distribution directly.
defects.after_excerpt: $$f(\Delta t) = a \exp\left(-a\,\Delta t\right)$$ where $a = \sum a_i$. ... use NumPy's exponential distribution with scale $=1/a$ (the mean waiting time, $a=\sum a_i$).
defects.rationale: Both before fragments are present in field_diffs.before (53.1 step_background PDF and 53.1 step_description_prompt). The original PDF f=(1/a)exp(-dt/a) has the rate inverted: it contradicts its own stated 'rate equal to the sum of all propensities a' and yields mean a instead of 1/a; the corrected f=a*exp(-a*dt) is the true exponential with rate a. The prompt's 'use NumPy's exponential directly' under-specified the scale; R3 ledger (before_in_original=true for both fields) confirms scale=1/a is load-bearing (seeded test compares exact time_step; scale=a fails by ~6 orders). One parameterization defect spanning two co-edited fields; correctly grouped. Direction too-strict/wrong: the wrong/under-specified spec would mislead a correct solver while gold/test enforce the correct exponential.

defects.subcategory: under-specified event-recording boundary convention (time < T)
defects.action: Added the load-bearing boundary clause 'record an event only if its time is strictly less than T' to the 53.2 prompt.
defects.before_excerpt: Record both the time coordinates and the evolution of populations. Identify which of the following ecological events occurred
defects.after_excerpt: Record both the time coordinates and the evolution of populations; record an event only if its time is strictly less than T. Identify which of the following ecological events occurred
defects.rationale: Anchored to field_diffs sub_steps[1].step_description_prompt: before is silent on whether an event whose time reaches/crosses T is recorded; after inserts 'record an event only if its time is strictly less than T'. R3 ledger (before_in_original=true) confirms this boundary is load-bearing: the seeded test compares time_cor exactly, so including/excluding the boundary event changes the array. The removed intermediate parenthetical '(do not record the event whose time reaches or crosses T)' is NOT in field_diffs.before, so correctly no separate defect is created for it. Direction too-strict/wrong: without the convention a correct simulation could legitimately disagree with the exact-array gold.

defects.subcategory: exact == on spectrally-estimated rounded period -> abs diff < 0.11
defects.action: Loosened the period comparison from exact equality (prey_period == e and predator_period == f) to a minimal tolerance (abs(prey_period - e) < 0.11 and abs(predator_period - f) < 0.11) across all three 53.4 test cases.
defects.before_excerpt: and prey_period == e and predator_period == f
defects.after_excerpt: and abs(prey_period - e) < 0.11 and abs(predator_period - f) < 0.11
defects.rationale: Anchored to field_diffs sub_steps[3].test_cases: all three cases change exact float equality on the period to abs(...) < 0.11. The periodicity is a spectral estimate over an unevenly sampled stochastic trajectory then rounded to one decimal place; exact == rejects a correct solution landing on an adjacent one-decimal bin (including a ceiling-vs-nearest difference at one decimal place, max ~0.1 < 0.11). The <0.11 band admits only the genuine one-decimal ambiguity while still rejecting wrong periods, matching the minimal tolerance-loosening principle.

defects.subcategory: Wrong/non-derivable SUPG tau convention + missing kappa; 54.3 mis-specified to re-add SUPG (double-count) and carried the same vestigial wrong-P^e tau bullet
defects.action: In problem_main, replaced the stated element-Peclet stabilization parameter (tau with P^e=|a|h/2kappa) with the gold-consistent fixed constant P=|a|=200 and added the missing kappa=1. In the 54.3 prompt, made the same fix coherently: removed the wrong/vestigial P^e tau bullet, added kappa=1, and clarified that stabilization() adds only the Nitsche boundary terms at x=1 (the SUPG volume term is already in assemble, so it is NOT added again here).
defects.before_excerpt: $\tau = \frac{h}{2|a|}(coth(P^e)-\frac{1}{P^e})$, where $P^e = \frac{|a|h}{2\kappa}$ is the element Peclet number. ... Write a function adjust mass matrix A and right hand side vector b, adding Nitsche term and SUPG stabilization term.
defects.after_excerpt: $\kappa = 1$ ... $\tau = \frac{h}{2|a|}(coth(P)-\frac{1}{P})$ with $P = |a| = 200$ ... adding the Nitsche boundary terms at $x=1$ ... it is NOT added again here.
defects.rationale: field_diffs.before for problem_main defines tau via the standard element Peclet number P^e=|a|h/2kappa and omits kappa as a parameter; the R4 ledger (before_in_original=true) verified the gold mass matrix A reproduces ONLY with the fixed P=|a|=200 and kappa=1, so a solver obeying the original spec computes a wrong-per-gold tau and is rejected. The 54.3 prompt (field_diffs entry #7, original->current) carried the identical wrong-P^e tau bullet AND said the function adds 'Nitsche term and SUPG stabilization term' which would double-count the SUPG volume term already assembled in 54.2; the after removes the tau bullet, adds kappa=1, and clarifies Nitsche-only. The ledger's before_in_original=false for the 54.3 entry refers to the R3 intermediate text, but field_diffs confirms the true-original 54.3 prompt did contain this wrong tau/SUPG wording, so it is anchored to a real original->current diff.

The R4 ledger (before_in_original=true) records that both models failed purely from the missing constants (pro NameError on undefined a/kappa/tau; flash guessed a=1,kappa=0.01) because the SciCode gencode harness does not feed problem_description_main to the model and these values live only there and in the later 54.3 step. A correct solver cannot derive a=200/kappa=1/P=200 from the 54.2 step text alone, so the original step wrongly forces failure. (Scoped to the 54.2 prompt field only; the related 54.3 prompt edit is owned by 54-d1 to avoid over-grouping one field's edit across defects.)

Genuine too-strict test bug.

defects.subcategory: wrong/under-specified physics convention (pairwise sum scope, displacement-vector type & sign, force accumulation)
defects.action: Corrected the 80.3 background from 'energy between the two atoms next to each other' to the sum over ALL distinct pairs (i<j) at the minimum-image distance; retyped f_ij's r from a scalar distance to the 3D minimum-image displacement vector r_j - r_i; and made forces() Returns explicit about the all-pairs accumulation f_xyz[i] += f_ij(d_ij), f_xyz[j] -= f_ij(d_ij).

defects.after_excerpt: The total potential energy is the sum over ALL distinct pairs of atoms (i<j) ... at the minimum-image distance, not just consecutive atoms. ... [f_ij] r (np.array): the 3D minimum-image displacement vector ... (r_j - r_i).
defects.rationale: All three sub-changes are present in field_diffs (80.3 step_background, 80.4 function_header r-type, 80.5 function_header Returns). The original background ('two atoms next to each other') describes only consecutive-pair energy, physically wrong for an LJ system and inconsistent with the gold O(N^2) pair sum; f_ij's r was mistyped as a scalar when the gold uses a signed 3D displacement; and forces() left the accumulation sign convention implicit. target_patch (r1, substeps 80.3/80.5/80.6) corroborates the gold convention fix. A correct solver could be penalized under the original under-/mis-specified convention: too-strict/wrong. The three share one convention-fix and group cleanly.
